newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close narrowly mixed.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed mixed in token volume Monday as players stood back from the market awaiting Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee, dealers said.

"Everybody is holding their bets until the Fed makes an announcement -- if it hikes rates prices may slip temporarily and if not the bolsa should continue to tick higher," said Andres Mc Ewan at trader Velox.
The blue-chip MerVal index posted its sixth consecutive small gain of 0.2 percent to 744.67, while the broad market eased 0.1 percent.
But floor volume dwindled to just 12.7 million pesos from 23.8 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover shrank to 65.3 million pesos from 125.5 million Friday.

"It was a given that we wouldn't see much action today," another trader said. "However, nobody here seems really worried -- it's more like they're taking a break and kind of amused, waiting to see how the north reacts to the Fed news."
Session winners edged out losers 26 to 24 and 14 issues closed unchanged.
Top main-tier performers were steelmaker Siderar, textile firm and shoemaker Alpargatas and holding company Comercial del Plata, which climbed 4.9 percent, 1.7 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.
Losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which shed 2.0 percent, Telefonica, down 1.1 percent, and construction stock Polledo, off 0.9 percent.
"One we get the Fed out of the way I think Argentina will attract fresh investments, especially if we see progress on privatizations and labor reforms," a foreign analyst said.
